== Problem ==
What is the value of <cmath>(2^2-2)-(3^2-3)+(4^2-4)</cmath>

<math>\textbf{(A) } 1 \qquad\textbf{(B) } 2 \qquad\textbf{(C) } 5 \qquad\textbf{(D) } 8 \qquad\textbf{(E) } 12</math>

== Solution 1==
<math>(4-2)-(9-3)+(16-4)=2-6+12=8.</math> This corresponds to <math>\boxed{\textbf{(D) } 8}.</math>

-happykeeper

== Solution 2==
We have
<cmath>\begin{align*}
\left(2^2-2\right)-\left(3^2-3\right)+\left(4^2-4\right) &= 2(2-1)-3(3-1)+4(4-1) \\
&= 2(1)-3(2)+4(3) \\
&= 2-6+12 \\
&= \boxed{\textbf{(D) } 8}.
\end{align*}</cmath>
~MRENTHUSIASM

==Solution 3 (Overkill: Just for Fun)==
We have
<cmath>\begin{align*}
(2^2-2)-(3^2-3)+(4^2-4) &= 2^2+4^2-3^2-2+3-4 \\
&=2^2+(4-3)(4+3)-3 \\
&=2^2+7-3=2^2+4 \\
&=4\cdot 2 \\
&=\boxed{\textbf{(D) } 8}.
\end{align*}</cmath>
-[[User:PureSwag|PureSwag]]

==Solution 4 (When you have too much time) ==

Using the difference of squares, we have <cmath>(2-\sqrt{2})(2+\sqrt{2}) - (3-\sqrt{3})(3+\sqrt{3}) + (4-2)(4+2).</cmath>
Knowing that <math>\sqrt{2} \approx 1.41</math> and <math>\sqrt{3} \approx 1.73,</math> we get <cmath>(2-\sqrt{2})(2+\sqrt{2}) - (3-\sqrt{3})(3+\sqrt{3}) + (4-2)(4+2) \approx 0.59\cdot 3.41 -1.26\cdot 4.73 + 2 \cdot 6
=8.0521,</cmath> which is closest to <math>\boxed{\textbf{(D) } 8}.</math>
